newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian shares ease as correction continues.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian shares ease as correction continues.

text.p: Slovenian SBI index eased nearly one percent on Wednesday as a correction continued for the second day, taking losses to a total of 2.5 percent after a 7.7 percent jump the previous week.

"International investors' demand is down as foreigners wait for half year results to make sure the prices are acceptable. If foreign demand remains low the index could drop to 1,500 points in the next couple of days," said Mili Kus, head of brokerage Eastbrokers.
* The SBI index fell 14.11 points to 1,544.29.
* Drug firm Lek was most actively traded, down 2.97 percent to 35,000 tolars on volume of 2,703 shares.

Traders said the fall was mainly due to a slump in international demand in Lek as most foreigners had already bought the Lek stock they wanted in their portfolio. International investors hold about 22 percent of the company. -- Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-125-8439
